Breadth advancers improved from 24 to 29 between captures, but this is a point-in-time proxy with changing membership, not confirmed canonical breadth.
Current funding is modestly positive for BTC and slightly negative for ETH; the supplied observations do not establish broadly excessive positive funding.
BTC and ETH ETF rows for 2026-10-07 are both net negative, but the observations are one settled session and do not establish a persistent flow trend.
Historical Action Compass calibration is explicitly low-confidence and descriptive. It reports retest watches, not validated exit rules or evidence that a current distribution event is occurring.
evidence_for: The direct hourly sequence is broadly negative across available horizons: BTC returned -2.23% over the 9-hour 12h window, -2.86% over the 21-hour 24h window, and -5.38% over the 69-hour 72h window; ETH returned -5.11%, -4.97%, and -10.14%, respectively.

ETH/BTC fell across those windows: -2.97% at 12h, -2.18% at 24h, and -5.06% at 72h. Direct hourly closes remain above 0.0300, but the latest close is only 0.03005 and the full 168-hour sequence has no closes below that level.

The latest point-in-time breadth capture has 29 advancers versus 70 decliners among 100 constituents. The separate earlier rich-breadth snapshot showed 24 advancers and 75 decliners; both are proxy-only and have different membership hashes.
CFGI reads Fear for BTC (26.5) and the market (23.5), and Extreme Fear for ETH (13).

Over 72 hours, open interest rose 7.85% for BTC and 9.01% for ETH despite negative returns; over the shorter 12- and 24-hour windows, reported OI changes were negative. This cross-horizon divergence does not resolve whether leverage is being added or reduced at the relevant point in the move.

The BlockchainCenter shadow rotation scores are 35 (30d), 43 (90d), and 37 (365d); its 90d score fell from 53 in the predecessor capture. CoinMarketCap's published 90d score is 53, leaving a 10-point methodology dispersion. Neither source confirms broad rotation.

This is more consistent with near-term deterioration risk than a confirmed re-acceleration, but the latest anchor capture shows a modest price rebound and improving advancer count, so a pullback/retest or pause remains possible. uncertainties: The 1-hour API horizon is unavailable because no anchor met the existing tolerance; the 4-hour-labelled window spans only 1 hour, so it is not a comparable four-hour return.
Hourly sequence windows are shorter than their nominal horizons: 9 hours for 12h, 21 hours for 24h, and 69 hours for 72h.
Latest mark-price and spot microstructure readings are later than the hourly sequence cutoff; the sequence and anchor therefore describe different observation times.
Latest breadth is proxy-only, uses point-in-time membership, and is not directly comparable to the earlier rich-breadth snapshot with a different membership hash.

Liquidation aggregates are lower bounds from a fragile legacy REST source with unverified completeness; options skew is a current-chain moneyness-bucket measure, not 25-delta skew, and lacks an equivalent historical snapshot.
Settled ETF evidence covers only the 2026-10-07 session; macro and legacy spot-owner data are unavailable in this capture.
The 12-hour and 168-hour historical calibration cohorts have low confidence, and their observed opportunity-cost and drawdown summaries do not establish current-event probabilities or decision rules.
